reviews.review: Made you feel like a Space Marine.
Good game for a 5 min blast

[h1]Overview[/h1]
[b]Warhammer: Space Marine[/b] (WHSM) is a [b]third-person action game[/b] developed by [i]Relic Entertainment[/i], set in the grim, war-torn future iconic of the 40K universe. Players will impersonate [b]Ultramarines captain Titus, called to defend a strategically vital Forge World[/b], where powerful Titans are manufactured, from an ensuing Ork invasion. What [b]initially seems a relatively normal mission for the Adeptus Astartes, soon turns out to be much more, involving even the ever deceitful Forces of Chaos[/b], threatening to destroy the entire planet. 

At the core, [b]WHSM plays out as a fast-paced action game[/b], featuring equally viable ranged and melee combat styles, good enemy variety, and a steady introduction of new weapons, powers and gadgets throughout its campaign, so [b]it never becomes stale but on the opposite, makes progression interesting[/b] as it changes enemy types, situations and equipment constantly. The way this game [b]depicts the grim, war-torn 40K universe is some of the best among this whole videogame franchise[/b], nailing the core concepts and atmosphere types that make this setting so unique. This title delivers solid, frequent third-person action with enough variety to keep it interesting, [b]despite combat mechanics not being very deep in comparison with other games of the same kind[/b], good campaign story, and [b]interesting secondary modes such as wave survival and PvP[/b], though not many players can be found nowadays.

Even with many good points in its favor, this game also has some flaws to note: [b]first of all, the decision to bind certain co-op skill unlocks to PvP achievements is bad[/b], considering some people [b]may not be interested in that aspect, and also that nowadays not many people still play this game[/b] in PvP, that means having content gated behind a game mode that isn't much used any longer. Secondly, [b]the few boss fights in the campaign are quite underwhelming[/b], with the final boss being a [b]quick time event sequence[/b] instead of an actual fight, which is very disappointing.

Overall, [b]Warhammer: Space Marine[/b] is a good third-person action game that [b]delivers an engaging albeit short campaign, a really fun co-op (or solo) survival mode, and a decent PvP oriented selection of modes[/b], the latter not being much played nowadays though. For [b]a default price of 20€, offering around 5-6 hours of content for the campaign, while at least double that for survival if one wants to unlock equip and level up classes, I still would suggest waiting for a sale before buying, since the game gets greatly discounted often[/b] and doesn't really offer enough to be worth full price, especially with online modes being almost deserted.

[h1]Rating:[/h1]
[b]Very Good[/b]

[h1]Pros & Cons[/h1]

🔵 [b]Pros[/b]
+ One of the best 40K universe depictions in this entire game franchise to date.
+ Engaging, fast-paced combat that despite being rather simplistic, does the job very well and creates a solid system.
+ Good variety of enemies, weapons, upgrades and accessories in both campaign and even more so in Survival. 
+ Decently tough on max. difficulty (Hard), players looking for a challenge will be mostly satisfied.
+ Good storyline with believable characters and events, in line with the 40K lore. 

🔴 [b]Cons[/b]
- Short campaign: only around 5-6 hours without much replay value.
- Online modes are nearly deserted nowadays, hard to find players to play with.
- The decision of tying Survival mode unlocks to PvP achievements is not a good design choice.
- Underwhelming boss fights, especially the last one, reduced to a pathetic quick time event sequence.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1912254609

[h1]In-Depth Breakdown[/h1]

🎮 [b]Gameplay Analysis[/b]
The gameplay of WHSM is divided into Exploration, Combat and Additional Modes. 

[b]Exploration[/b] is pretty linear in this game, with few open areas or secondary places, mostly just put there in order to contain a collectible Servo Skull, unlocking a recording to get a bit more lore insight. Mostly, players will roam streamlined sections, where the only path is the "main" one, encountering enemies often, while also being on the lookout for ammo, grenade and weapon caches scattered around the battlefield, especially useful when short of munitions. There are no secrets or proper side areas to speak of. The addition of some section on board vehicles or featuring Jump Packs varies the formula a bit more, and is a nice change of pace.

[b]Combat[/b] is the true core of the experience, offering distinct ranged and melee approaches and a variety of weapons to deliver the Emperor's justice to heretics. Melee combat features various iconic weapons such as Chainsword or Thunder Hammer, and a combo system, with 3 normal combos and 3 stun combos for each weapon, which mostly consist in pressing the attack button repeatedly and are not "complex" combos as in other games. Stunning enemies is a core part of the mechanics, as they can be Executed, making Titus regain a portion of his health, and the only for of healing aside from Fury Mode. Unlike in other games, performing executions still has the character vulnerable, so making one with a dozen enemies around can very well lead to death, this is a good mechanic that forces players to think more and not just spam executions. 

[b]Combat, Pt.2[/b] Stronger enemies need more complex Stun combos, even multiple times, to be stunned. Fury Mode is filled with delivering damage to enemies, and when triggered makes Titus much more powerful, regenerating health and making all his attacks stagger, very useful in the most dangerous situations, and to be used wisely. 
Ranged combat features as well a variety of weapons from the iconic Bolter to the more exotic Melta Gun, most of them carry limited ammo, refilled with field supply crates, except in case of special weapons, with far more rare ammo to counter their superior power. Especially later in the game ranged combat is preferable as enemies will become increasingly deadly and just going in melee against a dozen chaos marines with plasma guns isn't gonna cut it.
Overall the combat, which is the prime game mechanic, delivers in full what is to be expected from a good action game, with also considerable challenge at max. difficulty.

[b]Additional Modes[/b] consist in Survival, a wave-based mode with its own progression, where 1 to 3 players can fight the Ork and Chaos hordes in various maps, using many abilities and weapons not present in the main campaign and PvP. Survival is very interesting because the progression encourages replay-ability to make it progressively farther into waves, as characters become stronger and have more advanced equip. PvP modes are your run of the mill CTF, TDM and so on, but in a 40K fashion using the same combat system as the other modes. Good luck finding players.

🔩 [b]Performance Analysis[/b]
[u]PC Specs: RTX2080Ti, Ryzen 3900X, 32GB RAM DDR4[/u]
The game is pretty old and should run well on even low spec machines by today's standards. I have no stability, performance or other issues to report, with a solid 144FPS in 1440p constantly. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1912118711

[h1]Final Thoughts[/h1]
Overall, WHSM is a well fleshed out action game that delivers the true feeling of the 40K universe, a simple but functional combat system, and enough variety, additional modes to result interesting for a decent amount of time. Fans of the franchise are in for a sure-fire buy here, and also action fans should definitely try it.
